entries.body: You fill my thoughts constantly. Every song I hear, every activity I throw myself into, every second my mind drifts for a moment, you're there. It's strange how still everything suddenly feels, now that time used to fly by so fast. Everything moves slowly now, and there's endless time, endless empty space. You've always said I think I know best. Now I truly know something. I know you've known best the whole time, and that I should have listened. I've never been good at receiving love, even though I've always wanted to be. And you did try. I felt it so many times, and we had so many romantic, wonderful moments together that I'll never forget. If you ever held a little of your love back so you wouldn't seem too into me, I understand it completely. It's nothing I blame you for. It just makes me sad at myself, that I didn't make it feel safe enough to let all of it out. I love you with all my heart. But I understand why you hesitated. When you called last week to check if I was okay, I let myself believe for a moment it meant something special, until I realized that's just who you are. You would have done it for anyone. It's in everything you do, whether it's your sister, your mom, or your friends. I envy that way of seeing life, and I wish I could become the best at sending it back your way, because I'm sure you'd love to be on the receiving end of it too. When I came to say thank you and saw you again, I don't know how to describe what happened in me. It was as if all the time and distance between us had suddenly been crossed out, and I felt an infatuation I'd never felt before. Maybe that's the difference between ordinary infatuation and the one person meant for you: being in love on top of loving someone. I regret it so deeply. I regret that I didn't act on all of it before the time ran out. It's insane to think how little it would have taken. We could have just talked things through. I could have listened, understood, changed my behavior. And I know it takes a lot of repeating, and a lot of getting through to me, before something actually sinks in. I've held back, the whole time. Never truly let myself listen to your love and take it all in, even though again and again I've caught myself feeling so tender about your feelings after a bad moment, without being able to open my own and let yours all the way in. This morning I wrote you a letter. I can't remember the last time I handwrote anything. It was a difficult exercise, getting the most important things I wanted to tell you down on paper. Attempt after attempt to get everything in, and still it would never feel exhaustive enough about my feelings for you. I'm completely certain I want to spend the rest of my life with you. I've never in my life been this in love, and I want to give you room to teach me, so we become a kind of symbiosis, where we share feelings, vulnerability, and still have ridiculous, childish fun alongside it all. Fuck, I miss when we used to be silly together, babe <3

The thought that has filled my head most today is that love has no deadline. And I think that's exactly why I've been so bad at it. I've always been good at everything with a date on it. Deadlines, deliveries, things that have to be finished. Everything without a deadline, I postpone, as if it could wait. But love isn't something you deliver on time. Love is life. It's what every person deserves to have, with the one who makes them whole. I would rather live on a rock and share it with you than be a machine that meets every deadline, has success, and is empty inside. That's what I understood today. It can't wait. And yet I'm ready to wait for you as long as it takes, because you waited for me long before I understood it myself. The only thing that can't wait is that I begin. The rest I'll gladly wait for. I want to grow and mature in this part of me, so you can be just as proud of me here as you are of the way I am as a father, and of my work. It's you I want to build my whole family around. I won't postpone anymore, and I won't hide from my feelings for you. I love you, of course. And I've started making a game, which I hope you'll find fun and sweet :) You're not the only creative one of us two, babe <3

I'm away with my parents and Vitus in Aarhus. I'm sharing a room with Vitus. When I booked the rooms a few months ago, I was almost certain I'd need three and not two. Now it feels empty here, even though he's making noise constantly haha. We went out for steak, a proper Gio menu :) I still remember our first date like it was yesterday. I was so shy and so bad at English. It's wild how much better we've both gotten at English over the course of our relationship, how it just became a natural part of my everyday life, even though languages have always been one of my biggest weaknesses. I remember the main course I picked that first night, a dish I definitely didn't like, while your choice looked so much better. I remember the first bit of courage I found when I kissed you at the bar afterwards, on December 2nd. It was awkward, I was shy, but when you tucked your hair behind your ears, I was completely sold. Fuck, you're beautiful. And fuck, how I miss caressing your ears and seeing how sensual and turned on it always made you. I miss everything about you, and I still can't quite accept that you're not here with me. This morning I came really close to racing around the city to find you, but I also know it's not me who sets the pace anymore. I know I've hurt you, and indirectly the people around you. It makes me so sad when I think back on what you wrote last week about how you've been feeling. I hope that one day I get to go down on one knee in front of you. I've always known I wanted children, and early in life too. At the same time, I've always thought a wedding wasn't necessarily that important to me. Now I think of nothing but making you mine forever. I love you <3

Today we went to Den Gamle By ("The Old Town", an open-air museum in Aarhus with whole streets of old Danish houses and shops kept exactly as they were) and to ARoS, the big art museum. It is good to be away from everything for a while. Den Gamle By is genuinely impressive, and it brought back memories from going there as a kid. It is strange to return as an adult, now that my own childhood is also in a time capsule, Blockbuster and all. The whole day made me think about whether the time we live in actually makes us happy. Always having to be available, having a life offline and a life online, and somehow having to coordinate the two, choosing what to keep and what to drop, with all the options we have now. It made me think about how badass you actually are. You came from the other side of the world with two suitcases and started a life here, and you have been here a year now. I hope you never leave Denmark. It is good to feel you close, even though we are mentally further apart than we have ever been. That you made that choice says everything about you. You are brave, you work hard, and you see the world with far more hope than most people manage. I think it is your warmth that keeps you going. I often forgot to acknowledge where you come from, and how much more I should have done to make your memories here feel like something you would never want to leave. At ARoS I have to admit I am more of a fan of abstract painting than of installation art. The quiet it gives my overworked head, when I take the time to think my way into what the artist was doing with the marks on the paper, is good for the darker thoughts. It is easy to forget in daily life, and it is something I hope we will spend more time on. I still have the dream of living a different kind of life when I am older, with creativity, quiet and nature taking up most of the room. Preferably with you. I started writing a song about you. But I got stuck. It is hard to separate infatuation, grief and love when all of it has to fit in the same song. I ended up with filthy lines like "hendes appeal gør mig lang som hendes hjemland", meaning "her appeal makes me as 'long' as her home country", sitting next to longing ones like "savner at drømme mig væk i hendes brune øjne", meaning "I miss losing myself in her brown eyes", and the whole thing pulls in every direction, like the confused thoughts of my inner child who does not want to grow up and take responsibility. I still hope to finish it one day. When I do, it will be here, somewhere in your universe. What caught me most at ARoS was a work by Jenny Holzer called Truisms. Contradictory statements, and wherever I looked they reminded me of things I have got wrong. The ones I kept coming back to were "you have to hurt others to be extraordinary", "being sure of yourself means you are a fool", and "you must know where you stop and the world begins". I actually felt physically unwell once I started turning them over. Can it really be true that the only way to rise is to push someone down? That being sure of yourself is a sign of the opposite? I have always felt sure of myself, so the second one fits me well enough. But I think there is a difference between feeling sure about life and the basic things, and the thing that matters more, which is real love. I have never been in doubt about my love for you. I just did not know how to handle it. And that is where I have been a fool, because I did not see how good what we had could have been, if I had trusted myself and stayed in the moment more. The last one is the hardest. Because I do not want to stop where you begin. I think you are unbelievably strong. Your whole story, your courage, your love of life and your independence make you tougher than anyone I know. I love you <3
